_comment: Deliberately NOT named 'fixture.json' -- tests/contracts/test_gate_policy_is_shared.py globs tests/fixtures/**/fixture.json and its _QUANTUM_BY_SUFFIX has no 1000-quantum case; this file must not be discovered by that enumerator.
_schema_version_2: #1084. v1 carried ONE top-level `recipe` and no board key on the rows, so it described the RETIRED dx=80um board while `test` above names a test that has run the #931 board since the migration commits 44a69919 / fc4c39a4 / 6743863f. v2 adds `boards` (one recipe per board id) and a mandatory `board` key on every datum; the v1 rows are unchanged in content and carry board="pre931-dx80um-onewall". The top-level `recipe` is gone -- read boards[<id>].recipe. tests/locks/test_msl_z0_platform_datums.py now asserts boards[active_board].recipe.dx_m == the test module's live DX, so the ledger cannot silently point at a different board again.

pre931-dx80um-onewall.retired_by: #931 lattice ownership contract. The fixture migrated on 44a69919 / fc4c39a4 / 6743863f; none of them touched this ledger, which is the defect issue #1084 names.

recipe.trace_realization: one-cell PEC Box drawn to H_SUB+DX and realized as ONE wall under the pre-contract rasterizer. h_sub/dx = 254/80 = 3.175, so the substrate rasterized to FOUR cells and the strip sat at z = 320um over 254um of dielectric plus a 66um air gap -- the structure the test module's own comment calls 'not the intended board'.

printed_2dp_band.note: The band 2-dp rows on THIS board must fall in: the reference datum's spread 0.004607 printed at the test's 2-dp quantum, +-0.0002 (0.01 pp of print slack either side). It is an agreement check among 2-dp rows, not a claim about full-precision agreement -- see classification_policy.

pre931-dx80um-onewall.note: Every row tagged with this board id was measured BEFORE the #931 migration, on a trace realized as one wall. bounds_unchanged / derivation / attribution below were all derived on THIS board and are kept as the historical record. They are NOT re-derived on the active board under #1084.

b931-dxH3-sheet.active_since: #931 lattice ownership contract (fixture migration commits 44a69919, fc4c39a4, 6743863f)

recipe.trace_realization: zero-thickness PEC sheet Box((0,y_lo,H_SUB),(lx,y_hi,H_SUB)) -- one node plane, normal E through it live (lattice ownership contract #931 1.3). dx = h_sub/3 puts the laminate face ON a node line, so preflight reports the sheet realized at node plane 3, offset +0.000 cell.

printed_2dp_band.note: The band 2-dp rows on THIS board must fall in, centred on the board's FIRST record (VESSL 369367259284, the #931 re-measure the test docstring quotes). It is NOT an agreement claim: the full-precision rows on this board read 0.00048-0.00057 and sit far outside it. That disagreement is a recorded, classified fact in cross_platform_checks, not a tolerance to widen.

b931-dxH3-sheet.note: The board the named test actually runs and the gate actually binds. bounds_unchanged is still the pre-931 board's derivation: re-deriving MEASURED_SPREAD_ENVELOPE on this board is a PI decision (it would TIGHTEN the gate), and issue #1084 explicitly does not take it.

bounds_unchanged.note: Both bounds are single-sourced from tests/unit/sparams/test_msl_port_integration.py's MEASURED_SPREAD_ENVELOPE (via tests/_gate_policy.gate_from_envelope) and LEG_S11_BOUND -- this ledger imports them, it does not restate them.

classification_policy.note: POLICY, NOT measured: a same-commit cross-platform spread disagreement >= 0.05 percentage points is classified as platform variance; a shift entering between two same-platform (CI) runs across a commit window is classified as code drift. ON THE RETIRED pre931-dx80um-onewall BOARD the measured fact is narrower than this policy number -- no two of its datums share a commit, so cross-platform agreement there is demonstrated as two same-regime PAIRS, not at a fixed commit: pre-drift {dev 0.4607% @69a6956a, GitHub runner 0.46% @90c79d1d, 4 rfx/ commits apart} and post-drift {GitHub runner 0.47% @7f68f9fb and @8e004976, this pod 0.4676% @1f005d0d}. Agreement finer than the 0.01 pp / 0.01 ohm print quantum is NOT MEASURED. ON THE ACTIVE b931-dxH3-sheet BOARD (#1084, 2026-09-16) the policy DOES have a same-commit pair to apply: at c6788ef7 a CPU row and a GPU row differ by 0.00925 pp and a same-host runtime-stack control differs by 0.00216 pp. See cross_platform_checks for each comparison, its recomputable gap and its verdict.

attribution.result: TWO steps, not one. The recipe file itself is byte-identical across the whole window (md5 9faeeba500da9ced30baca8c6d939a04 at 69a6956a, 90c79d1d, 7f68f9fb, 1f005d0d), so the drift is rfx/ code.
attribution.method: per-sha git-archive trees, one process each, driven by that tree's own _run_msl_thru; see the role="bisect" datums below and tests/fixtures/msl_z0_length_invariance/bisect_796.json for the raw per-leg dump.

commits.subject: extend static materials into the CPML pad for domain-face-touching boxes (closes #627)
commits.mechanism: this fixture's substrate Box((0,0,0)-(lx,LY,H_SUB)) is flush with the x-lo/x-hi/y-lo/y-hi domain faces, all CPML. #638 lets a hi-face pad whose naive interior-edge source column reads vacuum source from the column one further in, so the x-hi/y-hi pads went from eps_r=1 to eps_r=EPS_R -- the absorber stops being mismatched against the substrate it terminates.

commits.subject: give the boundary node the material its own pad already gets (closes #655)
commits.mechanism: #638 wrote the recovered material into the pad only, leaving the dropped boundary node vacuum -- a one-cell film between the structure and its own matched absorber. #659 writes the replicated value into the outermost interior column too.

attribution.classification: i -- both are intended absorber-matching corrections with their own measured witnesses (#638: its secondary 'author's independent fixture' witness, edge-touching-slab tail/peak energy -85.15 dB -> -90.62 dB — the PR's headline absorber witness is -95.63 -> -104.25 dB; #659: reflection off the one-cell vacuum film 0.2375 -> exactly 0.0 at the default mesh). Neither is a regression, so the shift is a better-terminated board, not a defect to revert.
attribution.bit_identity_chain: leg-8 mean|Z0[+x]| on the bisect platform: 90c79d1d = ae7919a9 = 57.33811569213867; fce10916 = 5f23ccae = fd37c62f = 57.33358383178711; c9c1864f = 7f68f9fb = 1f005d0d = 57.32954406738281. Legs 10 and 12 follow the same three-value chain.
attribution.corrects: The 2026-09-13 close comment named 7f68f9fb (#666, the x/y axis generalization of add_msl_port) as the only direct MSL-extraction change in the window and closed the issue as superseded by #931. Measurement says #666 moves nothing on this fixture: 7f68f9fb is bit-identical to its parent c9c1864f on all three legs. #645 and #658 (the two dtype lifts) are excluded the same way. The drift sits in #638 and #659.
attribution.gate_disposition: Bisect rows are tagged PASSED so tests/locks/test_msl_z0_platform_datums.py::test_every_passed_datum_is_actually_under_bound checks their recomputation (spread < 0.007, L=12 mean|S11| < 0.15). UNCHANGED and left to the PI. MEASURED_SPREAD_ENVELOPE stays 0.004607 and the enforced gate stays gate_from_envelope(0.004607, quantum=1000) = 0.007. gate_from_envelope(0.004686, quantum=1000) would derive 0.008 -- a ONE-QUANTUM WIDENING, which issue #610's no-silent-loosening rule forbids applying as routine maintenance even when the drift is attributed and benign. Re-deriving the envelope off the post-#638/#659 board is a PI decision, and on current main it would additionally have to be taken on the #931 board, not this one.
attribution.platform_variance_check: this host reads spread 0.4686% at 1f005d0d where the ledger's pod row (jax 0.6.2) reads 0.4676% -- 0.001 pp apart, far inside classification_policy.threshold_pp = 0.05, so the two platforms agree and the steps above are code.

cross_platform_checks.question: Is the gated board's spread platform-dependent between CPU and GPU at ONE commit?
cross_platform_checks.note: Both rows are the same git-archive tree at c6788ef7, x64 off, complex64. The gap is 0.0093 pp, far inside classification_policy.threshold_pp = 0.05, so by the ledger's own rule CPU and GPU AGREE on this board. That is the measurement #1084 asked for, and it rules the GPU backend out as the source of the 0.11 pp disagreement with the docstring row.

cross_platform_checks.question: Why does the docstring/VESSL 369367259284 row read 0.16% where every full-precision row on this board reads ~0.05%?
cross_platform_checks.note: classification_policy classifies a SAME-COMMIT cross-platform disagreement. These two rows do not share a recorded commit: run 369367259284's own `git rev-parse HEAD` printed 'no git', so its tree is known only as branch feat/931-t2-sparams-ports on 2026-09-07. The policy therefore cannot be applied, and this gap is recorded UNCLASSIFIED rather than called platform variance. What the same-commit rows do say: CPU and GPU agree (cpc-1084-cpu-vs-gpu), and the stack control (cpc-1084-stack-control) answers the runtime-stack half. Neither backend nor runtime stack explains the 0.16%, so what is left is the TREE that run measured -- the pre-merge feat/931-t2-sparams-ports branch. Settling it needs that sha, and the run log does not carry it.

cross_platform_checks.question: Does run 369367259284's runtime stack (jax[cpu] 0.6.2, numpy<2) reproduce its 0.16% on today's tree?
cross_platform_checks.note: Host, tree and recipe held fixed against cpu-epyc9654-c6788ef7-b931; only jax/numpy swapped to the docstring row's (jax 0.6.2, jaxlib 0.6.2, numpy 1.26.4). The two differ by 0.00216 pp, inside classification_policy.threshold_pp = 0.05, so the runtime stack AGREES and does not explain the docstring row's 0.16%. This control sits 0.11012 pp from that row. With backend (cpc-1084-cpu-vs-gpu) and stack both excluded at a fixed commit, the remaining candidate is the TREE run 369367259284 measured -- the pre-merge feat/931-t2-sparams-ports branch, whose sha it did not record.
